slices.focus: Tasha discovers fiction reading as evening decompression after Imani's book swap
slices.summary: Tasha shares how a low-pressure evening at Imani's apartment — soup, ordinary conversation, and borrowed contemporary Southern novels — led to a meaningful change in her bedtime routine. She had been reading only grief-related material at night, which made her feel like she never left work. The fiction stack from Imani's library discard shelf became an evening reset tool, helping her jaw unclench and her mind stop racing. The agent helps her recognize this as adjusting (not avoiding) and suggests a two-week experiment of fiction-first bedtime reading with heavier books moved out of reach.
